articles.title: Ramayana Crosses ₹1,500 Crore Worldwide in 14 Days, Fifth Indian Film to Reach the Mark
articles.excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's epic reached ₹1,519.05 crore worldwide on Day 14 — ₹1,009.05 crore gross in India and ₹510 crore overseas — making Tiwari the only Indian director with two ₹1,500 crore global hits, according to Sacnilk.
articles.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor as Ram, hands folded, in a still from Ramayana.
articles.nri_angle: The film's ₹510 crore overseas run — an all-time first-phase international record for an Indian film — was powered substantially by diaspora audiences.

articles.title: GTA 6 Unlocks in India After 13-Year Wait; US Players Get It at Midnight
articles.excerpt: Rockstar's rolling midnight launch opened in India at 12:00 a.m. IST on November 19 and reaches the US West Coast last. India pricing starts at ₹5,999, the download runs to 212 GB, and there is no PC version at launch.
articles.image_caption: Artwork from Rockstar Games' first Grand Theft Auto VI trailer announcement. GTA VI unlocked in India on November 19, more than 13 years after GTA V.
articles.nri_angle: The rolling midnight launch means Indian players unlocked hours before the US, where diaspora players get the game at midnight local time on November 19.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pallavi Paul's 'How Love Moves' Wins $25,000 Al Jazeera Award at IDFA Forum
articles.excerpt: The New Delhi graveyard documentary took the Al Jazeera Documentary Co-Production Award at IDFA's industry market in Amsterdam, with the jury praising its political and creative sophistication.
articles.image_caption: A still from Pallavi Paul's documentary How Love Moves, set in a century-old graveyard in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: IDFA is the world's leading documentary festival; an Indian project winning its market's co-production award is how Indian non-fiction reaches international screens and diaspora audiences.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nawazuddin Siddiqui's 'Dr. Hassan' Brings 'House' to India, Premieres December 11 on JioHotstar
articles.excerpt: JioHotstar has released the teaser for its Hindi adaptation of the Hugh Laurie medical drama, with Dia Mirza as the hospital chief and Rohan Sippy directing.
articles.image_caption: Nawazuddin Siddiqui as Dr. Hassan and Dia Mirza in a still from the series Dr. Hassan.
articles.nri_angle: House ran for eight seasons on US network television; its Hindi adaptation gives diaspora viewers a familiar format rebuilt with Indian characters, conversations and humour.

articles.title: Prince William Gets a Bollywood Welcome at Karan Johar's Dharma Productions
articles.excerpt: Dancers performed ‘Shava Shava’ from Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham as Karan Johar, Kareena Kapoor Khan and Saif Ali Khan hosted the Prince of Wales on the final morning of his Mumbai visit.
articles.image_caption: Prince William with Karan Johar, Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor Khan at Dharma Productions in Mumbai. The studio visit, on the final morning of the royal couple's India tour, featured a dance performance of Shava Shava from Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham.
articles.nri_angle: Bollywood's British thread runs through the diaspora: K3G was partly filmed in Britain, its stars shoot in London several times a year, and the prince's studio stop was aimed at the UK-India creative-industries link.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ‘Varuvaaiy’ Becomes First Tamil Song Ever Nominated for a Grammy Award
articles.excerpt: Devan Ekambaram and Susha’s contemporary setting of a Subramania Bharati devotional poem is shortlisted for Best Global Music Performance at the 69th Grammys, alongside Shakira, Burna Boy and Rosalía.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian American composer’s Tamil bhajan reaching the Grammys’ global shortlist is a first for Tamil music and a landmark for the diaspora’s Carnatic tradition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ramayana Becomes First Bollywood Film to Cross Rs 50 Crore in Kerala
articles.excerpt: Trade trackers estimate the Hindi epic passed Rs 50 crore gross in Kerala in its second week, nearly 160% above the previous Bollywood record, and the milestone makes Yash the first actor to open the state's 50-crore club for two industries.
articles.nri_angle: A Hindi epic crossing Rs 50 crore in Kerala — powered in part by Yash's Ravana — is the kind of cross-industry run diaspora audiences are tracking worldwide.

articles.nri_angle: The film's Oscar campaign runs through Los Angeles, where it has already screened for diaspora and Academy audiences.

articles.title: Ramayana Passes Dhurandhar 2's 11-Day Worldwide Record, Tracker Estimates Show
articles.excerpt: Sacnilk's updated tally puts Ramayana at an estimated ₹1,384.50 crore worldwide after 11 days, with India net at ₹760.60 crore — though the tracker figures are still being revised.
articles.nri_angle: An estimated ₹499.43 crore of the worldwide gross has come from overseas markets, underlining how strongly diaspora audiences have turned out for the epic.

articles.title: Scene Review: Suriya's Loose, Playful Cop Act Carries an Uneven Crime Comedy
articles.excerpt: A star performance worth the ticket, wrapped around a cold case that never quite earns its finale.
articles.image_caption: Suriya at the audio launch of Retro. The Tamil actor stars as a police officer in Jithu Madhavan's Scene. Photo: Shiva CK / Wikimedia Commons.
articles.nri_angle: The film is available with subtitles, making it accessible for non-Tamil speakers, and offers a unique blend of humor and action that may resonate well with fans of Suriya.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.rating_consensus: Suriya's loosest, most playful performance in years carries a crime comedy whose jokes land harder than its investigation — charming and inventive in stretches, uneven in pace, and let down by a climax that doesn't cash its buildup.

articles.title: Why Yash's Own Kannada Voice Makes His Ravana Land Harder Than the Hindi Dub
articles.excerpt: Sharad Kelkar voices Ravana for Hindi audiences in Ramayana: Part 1 — and does it well. But critics who have seen both versions say Yash's own pauses and intonation in Kannada are part of the performance no dub can fully recreate.
articles.image_caption: Yash at the trailer launch of Toxic. In Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part 1, Yash plays Ravana and voices the role himself in the Kannada version.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora viewers choosing a screening, the version matters: the Kannada cut carries Yash's own voice as Ravana, while the Hindi cut uses Sharad Kelkar — a genuine choice, now playing out in the film's record run.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Imtiaz Ali Says 'Dhurandhar' Was Called Impractical — Now Everyone Wants to Make It
articles.excerpt: At the HT Leadership Summit, the filmmaker said Bollywood dismissed Aditya Dhar's Ranveer Singh spy thriller as the film least likely to succeed; the franchise has since grossed over Rs 3,000 crore worldwide.
articles.image_caption: Ranveer Singh in a still from Dhurandhar, Aditya Dhar's Hindi spy thriller. Filmmaker Imtiaz Ali told the HT Leadership Summit the film was dismissed as impractical before the franchise passed Rs 3,000 crore worldwide.
articles.nri_angle: The first Dhurandhar earned $33 million overseas; Ali's remarks frame the franchise as the new reference point for Hindi films built to play to India and the diaspora at once.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Giri Babu, Telugu Cinema's Versatile Face of Five Decades, Dies at 80
articles.excerpt: Born Yerra Seshagiri Rao, the actor moved from hero to villain to beloved character artiste across more than 600 Telugu films, and also produced and directed.
articles.image_caption: Telugu actor Giri Babu in a file photograph. The veteran of more than 600 films died at a private hospital in Hyderabad on Saturday, aged 80.
articles.nri_angle: Giri Babu's 600-plus Telugu films spanned the decades when Telugu cinema became a fixture for diaspora audiences worldwide; his son Raghu Babu remains a familiar face in the industry today.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ramayana Posts Record Second Friday, Second-Biggest Ever for a Hindi Film
articles.excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's epic collected about Rs 47 crore nett across India on its second Friday — a record for the day — while its Hindi version's Rs 36 crore ranked second only to Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
articles.nri_angle: The film's hold in its second week is the figure North American exhibitors watch when deciding how long to keep the epic on diaspora screens.

articles.title: Ramayana Crosses Rs 1,000 Crore Worldwide in Eight Days, Third-Fastest Indian Film Ever
articles.excerpt: Sacnilk puts the worldwide gross at Rs 1,033.55 crore, with India net at Rs 564.60 crore — already beyond the lifetime domestic totals of Pathaan and Animal.
articles.image_caption: Sai Pallavi at the launch event for Ramayana. The Ranbir Kapoor-led epic crossed Rs 1,000 crore worldwide in eight days, the third-fastest Indian film to reach the mark.
articles.nri_angle: The film opened at number one in the UK and Ireland and is drawing diaspora audiences in North America in its theatrical run, with no streaming date announced in the Day 8 reports.

articles.title: Mookuthi Amman 2: Critics Say Nayanthara's Star Power Can't Save This Overstuffed Sequel
articles.excerpt: A mixed reception highlights the film's visual ambition but weak storytelling.
articles.nri_angle: The film is available with subtitles, making it accessible for diaspora audiences, although it may require some cultural context to fully appreciate its themes.

articles.title: Bollywood Bolsters Security as Shootings Revive Underworld Fears
articles.excerpt: After gunfire at Tiger Shroff's car and a wave of extortion threats linked to the Bishnoi gang, stars are hiring bodyguards, police are telling actors to avoid crowds, and the industry is arguing over whether the 1990s are really back.
articles.image_caption: Actor Tiger Shroff at a public appearance in Mumbai. Gunfire targeted Shroff's car in the Juhu area on October 18, and police have arrested 13 people in connection with the attack.
articles.nri_angle: The threats target the stars diaspora audiences watch most; tighter security is already changing fan-facing events and public appearances around film promotions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kunal Kemmu's Hindi Comedy Vibe Arrives on Prime Video November 13
articles.excerpt: Kunal Kemmu's Hindi action-comedy Vibe, co-starring Preity G Zinta and Sparsh Shrivastava, premieres on Prime Video on November 13, 2026 after a September theatrical run. It is Kemmu's second film as director, after Madgaon Express.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora viewers can stream this new Hindi film on Prime Video from November 13, 2026, with a subscription, as reported by the sources read.

articles.title: Kareena Kapoor Khan Gets Legal Notice Over Quranic Verse Pendant Worn for Diwali
articles.excerpt: Reports say Abbas Hafeez sent a legal notice to Kareena Kapoor Khan and stylist Rhea Kapoor asking for Diwali photographs showing an emerald pendant inscribed with Ayat-ul-Kursi to be removed and for an apology — a demand, not a court finding.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora Bollywood audiences, the story is a reported dispute over religious inscription, family heirloom jewellery and festive social media presentation, stated without treating an allegation as a finding.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bollywood Romance 'Weekend' Eyes First Indian Feature Shoot in Russia's Yakutia
articles.excerpt: Producer Vivek Singhania's Picture Perfect has signed a three-way MoU with Saidam Baryl and Sakhafilm, Yakutia's state-backed studio, to explore shooting the romantic drama in the Sakha Republic — a first for an Indian feature.
articles.image_caption: Yhyakh is a New Year celebration in Sakha Republic (Yakutia). The Bollywood romantic drama Weekend is eyeing a shoot in Russia's Sakha Republic, known as Yakutia, after producer Vivek Singhania's Picture Perfect signed a memorandum of understanding with local outfits Saidam Baryl and Sakhafilm.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Tenebroid via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: An Indian production exploring a first-ever feature shoot in Yakutia extends Bollywood's long, Soviet-era popularity in Russia's far east to a new frontier.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
